scope: Proposition 4.4 (Local exclusion of opposite intersection signs) of the manuscript “The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers” (preprints/The-curve-scaling-limit-of-half-plane-double-dimers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 226 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e1bcd39145db94c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let u be either the horizontal or vertical coordinate, let L = {u = c} be a test line, and let J ⊂ L be a bounded segment. If u is the vertical coordinate, assume c > 0. Fix a bounded window K ⊂ H and buffers ρ−, ρ+ > 0. Deterministically partition J into O(h−1) intervals of length at most h, with endpoints off the graph. Let Eδ,h be the event that, for one of these intervals I, one directed half-plane cycle has two portions α, β contained in K such that each portion has one endpoint in {u ≤ c − ρ−} and the other in {u ≥ c + ρ+}, and ιI(α)ιI(β) < 0. Then lim h↓0 lim sup δ↓0 P(Eδ,h) = 0. (34) For a vertical line L, the segment may reach or extend below the bottom boundary. Test lines are chosen off lattice vertices; the same estimate holds for seam perturbations of order δ.
